subject.title: [Feature]: Allow job-level model override for cron jobs using sessionTarget=main + payload.kind=systemEvent

question: Should main-session systemEvent cron jobs gain a supported model/provider override contract, and if so should the contract be payload.model, job-level model/provider fields, or an explicit sessionOverride block?
rationale: Source inspection proves the gap, but the fix changes public cron schema, model/provider precedence, persisted payload behavior, and main-session state semantics, which requires maintainer product/API intent.

options.title: Extend systemEvent payload.model
options.body: Add payload.model to systemEvent as the narrowest contract matching agentTurn, with allowlist validation and run-scoped session override behavior.

options.title: Add job-level override shape
options.body: Introduce model/provider or sessionOverride at the job level so multiple payload kinds share one explicit override contract, at the cost of a broader schema surface.

options.title: Keep systemEvent text-only
options.body: Document isolated agentTurn jobs as the supported model-controlled cron path and leave main-session systemEvent jobs on the session default.

recommendation.title: Extend systemEvent payload.model
recommendation.body: Add payload.model to systemEvent as the narrowest contract matching agentTurn, with allowlist validation and run-scoped session override behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available routing signal is prior merged work around cron model override semantics and isolated cron execution seams, plus the decision cuts across runtime and API boundaries.
